message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s usually handled by the city’s police department or code‑enforcement office rather than the city council itself.** Below is a quick guide on how to do it and what to expect. --- ## 1. Who handles noise complaints? | Agency | Typical role | Contact | |--------|--------------|---------| | **Atlanta Police Department (APD)** | First line of response; can issue citations for violations of the city’s noise ordinance. | Phone: **404‑656‑4000** (non‑emergency)
Email: **noise@atlantaga.gov** | | **City of Atlanta Code Enforcement** | Handles ongoing or repeated violations, may conduct inspections, and can refer cases to APD. | Phone: **404‑656‑4000** (same as APD)
Email: **code@atlantaga.gov** | | **City Council** | Can review complaints that have escalated or involve broader policy issues, but they rarely act on individual noise complaints directly. | Contact your council member via the city website. | > **Tip:** If you’re dealing with a one‑off nuisance, start with the APD. For repeated or persistent problems, the code‑enforcement office is the right place. --- ## 2. How to file a complaint ### A. Online (recommended) 1. **Visit the 311 portal** - URL: - Select “Noise” or “Public Safety” → “Noise Complaint.” 2. **Fill out the form** - Provide your name, address, phone number, and a brief description of the noise (time, duration, source, decibel level if known). 3. **Submit** - You’ll receive a confirmation number and an estimated response time. ### B. By Phone - Call **404‑656‑4000** (non‑emergency line). - Tell the operator you want to file a noise complaint. - They’ll ask for details and give you a reference number. ### C. In Person - Visit the **City Hall** at **101 Marietta Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30303**. - Go to the “Public Safety” or “Code Enforcement” desk. - Fill out a paper complaint form. ### D. By Email - Send an email to **noise@atlantaga.gov** or **code@atlantaga.gov**. - Include all relevant details and attach any supporting evidence (photos, audio recordings, etc.). --- ## 3. What happens next? 1. **Initial assessment** – APD will determine if the noise violates the city’s ordinance (see § 13‑1‑1‑1 of the Atlanta Noise Ordinance). 2. **Response** – Officers may issue a warning or citation. 3. **Follow‑up** – If the problem persists, the code‑enforcement office may conduct inspections or refer the case to the APD for further action. 4. **Appeal** – If you receive a citation, you can appeal it in court or request a hearing before the city council if the matter escalates. --- ## 4. Quick reference: Atlanta Noise Ordinance (simplified) | Time | Allowed Decibel Level | Typical Violations | |------|-----------------------|--------------------| | 7 AM–10 PM | 70 dB (daytime) | Loud music, construction, barking dogs | | 10 PM–7 AM | 55 dB (nighttime) | Same as above, plus amplified sound, parties | > *Note:* These limits apply to residential areas. Commercial zones may have different thresholds. --- ## 5. Need more help? - **City of Atlanta – 311**: - **Atlanta Police Department – Noise Complaints**: - **City Council Contact**: Find your council member on the city website and email them directly if you feel the issue needs higher-level attention. --- ### Bottom line You can definitely file a noise complaint in Atlanta. Start with the Atlanta Police Department or the city’s code‑enforcement office, use the online portal or phone line, and follow up as needed. The city council can intervene if the situation escalates or if you believe there’s a broader policy concern.
